findings.summary: Async IndexedDB write (db.drafts.put) is invoked from inside the React state updater function passed to setSets, violating the requirement that updater functions be pure.
findings.mechanism: React may invoke a functional state updater more than once for a single logical update (StrictMode double-invoke, or a render that is started, discarded, and retried under concurrent rendering/automatic batching). Each invocation fires db.drafts.put as a side effect during the render phase, not just on commit — so a discarded/replayed render still performs a real, externally-visible IndexedDB write even though its resulting state is thrown away. The comment claims this is harmless because the write is 'idempotent', but that only holds if every invocation is passed the same `s` snapshot; if a stale or discarded render invokes the updater with an older `s`, the draft can be (harmlessly transiently, but non-deterministically) written with a stale value before the real update reruns.
